/**\n514\t   * Format date for display\n515\t   */\n516\t  private formatDate(timestamp: number): string {\n517\t    const date = new Date(timestamp);\n518\t    const now = new Date();\n519\t    const diffMs = now.getTime() - date.getTime();\n520\t    const diffMins = Math.floor(diffMs / 60000);\n521\t    const diffHours = Math.floor(diffMs / 3600000);\n522\t    const diffDays = Math.floor(diffMs / 86400000);\n523\t\n524\t    if (diffMins < 1) {\n525\t      return 'just now';\n526\t    } else if (diffMins < 60) {\n527\t      return `${diffMins} minute${diffMins > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;\n528\t    } else if (diffHours < 24) {\n529\t      return `${diffHours} hour${diffHours > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;\n530\t    } else if (diffDays < 7) {\n531\t      return `${diffDays} day${diffDays > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;\n532\t    } else {\n533\t      return date.toLocaleDateString();\n534\t    }\n535\t  }\n536\t\n537\t  /**\n538\t   * Toggle the file list visibility\n539\t   */\n540\t  private async toggleFileList(): Promise<void> {\n541\t    await this.fileListUI.toggle();\n542\t    this.updateFileListButtonState();\n543\t  }\n544\t\n545\t  /**\n546\t   * Update the file list button state based on visibility\n547\t   */\n548\t  private updateFileListButtonState(): void {\n549\t    const isVisible = this.fileListUI.isPanelVisible();\n550\t    this.fileListToggleButton.innerHTML = isVisible ? ${diagnosis.confidence === 'low' ? The sending device reads a local file and flashes it out as an animated\n7\tsequence of optical codes. The receiving device runs the *same* web app, points\n8\tits camera at the sender's screen, decodes the frames, and reassembles the\n9\toriginal file byte-for-byte.\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\t┌─────────────────┐                      ┌─────────────────┐\n13\t│    SENDER       │   ░▓█ optical ░▓█    │    RECEIVER     │\n14\t│                 │  ──────────────────► │                 │\n15\t│  file → chunks  │  animated code frames│  frames → file  │\n16\t│  → coded frames │   screen to camera   │  → download     │\n17\t└─────────────────┘                      └─────────────────┘\n18\t        same static web app on both ends\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tAnimated QR codes are the obvious way to do this, and the likely starting point —\n22\tbut the goal is the *channel*, not the format. QR spends most of its capacity on\n23\trobustness screenferry doesn't need (arbitrary angles, print damage, one bit per\n24\tmodule). Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\n25\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\n26\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\n27\t\n28\t## Why\n29\t\n30\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\n31\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\n32\t\n33\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\n34\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\n35\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\n36\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\n37\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\n38\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\n39\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\n40\t\n41\t## The hard part\n42\t\n43\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\n44\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\n45\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\n46\tlooking away.\n47\t\n48\tA naive \"loop through chunks 1..N forever\" transfer degrades badly under loss\n49\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\n50\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\n51\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\n52\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. screenferry\\n2\\t\\n3\\t**Move a file between two devices using nothing but a screen and a camera.**\\n4\\t\\n5\\tscreenferry is a static web app — no server, no backend, no network between the two\\n6\\tdevices. Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\\n25\\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\\n26\\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\\n27\\t\\n28\\t## Why\\n29\\t\\n30\\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\\n31\\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\\n32\\t\\n33\\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\\n34\\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\\n35\\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\\n36\\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\\n37\\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\\n38\\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\\n39\\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\\n40\\t\\n41\\t## The hard part\\n42\\t\\n43\\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\\n44\\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\\n45\\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\\n46\\tlooking away.\\n47\\t\\n48\\tA naive \\\"loop through chunks 1..N forever\\\" transfer degrades badly under loss\\n49\\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\\n50\\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\\n51\\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\\n52\\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. Miss a frame and it simply doesn't\\n53\\tmatter — the next one is just as useful.\\n54\\t\\n55\\t## Status\\n56\\t\\n57\\t**Research complete. Phase 1 core codec built (22 tests green). Phase 0 harness and Phase 0.5 spike both partial** — see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) §17.2.\\n58\\t\\n59\\t- [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) — the complete application plan\\n60\\t- [`docs/notes/`](docs/notes/) — design decisions and constraints specific to screenferry\\n61\\t- [`docs/research/`](docs/research/) — findings:\\n62\\t  - `qr-encoding-capacity.md` — QR versions, EC levels, bytes per frame, JS encoders\\n63\\t  - `browser-qr-scanning.md` — camera capture, decoder libraries, binary safety\\n64\\t  - `fountain-codes-and-protocol.md` — erasure coding for a one-way channel, wire format\\n65\\t  - `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` — color barcodes, screen-camera research, what beats QR\\n66\\t  - `custom-codec-engineering.md` — feasibility of a purpose-built codec in a browser\\n67\\t  - `pwa-platform-and-ux.md` — offline PWA, file I/O, iOS constraints, UX, testing\\n68\\t\\n69\\t## Expectations\\n70\\t\\n71\\tThis is not a fast pipe. Realistic throughput is on the order of **kilobytes per\\n72\\tsecond** — good for keys, configs, documents, and small archives; not for video.\\n73\\tThe app is designed to be honest about this up front rather than let a user start\\n74\\ta transfer that would take an hour.\\n75\\t\\n76\\t## screenferry\\n2\\t\\n3\\t**Move a file between two devices using nothing but a screen and a camera.**\\n4\\t\\n5\\tscreenferry is a static web app — no server, no backend, no network between the two\\n6\\tdevices. Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\\n25\\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\\n26\\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\\n27\\t\\n28\\t## Why\\n29\\t\\n30\\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\\n31\\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\\n32\\t\\n33\\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\\n34\\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\\n35\\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\\n36\\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\\n37\\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\\n38\\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\\n39\\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\\n40\\t\\n41\\t## The hard part\\n42\\t\\n43\\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\\n44\\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\\n45\\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\\n46\\tlooking away.\\n47\\t\\n48\\tA naive \\\"loop through chunks 1..N forever\\\" transfer degrades badly under loss\\n49\\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\\n50\\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\\n51\\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\\n52\\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. Miss a frame and it simply doesn't\\n53\\tmatter — the next one is just as useful.\\n54\\t\\n55\\t## Status\\n56\\t\\n57\\t**Research complete. Phase 1 core codec built (22 tests green). Phase 0 harness and Phase 0.5 spike both partial** — see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) §17.2.\\n58\\t\\n59\\t- [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) — the complete application plan\\n60\\t- [`docs/notes/`](docs/notes/) — design decisions and constraints specific to screenferry\\n61\\t- [`docs/research/`](docs/research/) — findings:\\n62\\t  - `qr-encoding-capacity.md` — QR versions, EC levels, bytes per frame, JS encoders\\n63\\t  - `browser-qr-scanning.md` — camera capture, decoder libraries, binary safety\\n64\\t  - `fountain-codes-and-protocol.md` — erasure coding for a one-way channel, wire format\\n65\\t  - `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` — color barcodes, screen-camera research, what beats QR\\n66\\t  - `custom-codec-engineering.md` — feasibility of a purpose-built codec in a browser\\n67\\t  - `pwa-platform-and-ux.md` — offline PWA, file I/O, iOS constraints, UX, testing\\n68\\t\\n69\\t## Expectations\\n70\\t\\n71\\tThis is not a fast pipe. Realistic throughput is on the order of **kilobytes per\\n72\\tsecond** — good for keys, configs, documents, and small archives; not for video.\\n73\\tThe app is designed to be honest about this up */\n943\t  private isTransferConverging(): boolean {\n944\t    if (this.rateHistory.length < 5) return true; // Not enough data\n945\t\n946\t    // Check if rate is declining (bad sign)\n947\t
